instruction: Create a new sheet named "Rates" and in that sheet, merge cells A1:D1 to write "Interest Rate Comparison".

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a new sheet 'Rates' with A1:D1 merged containing 'Interest Rate Comparison'. Evaluator verifies: (1) Sheet 'Rates' exists, (2) A1:D1 are merged, (3) A1 contains the correct text.

llm_judge_reasons: Merge verification logic is fundamentally flawed: 'merge_start in ws.merged_cells' uses incorrect syntax as ws.merged_cells is a set of MergedCellRange objects, not strings
The isinstance(cell, MergedCell) check will fail for A1 since it's the top-left cell of the merge (regular Cell, not MergedCell in openpyxl)
Logic doesn't verify the exact merge range A1:D1 - it only checks if A1 is part of any merged region, so merging A1:B1 would incorrectly pass
The merge detection will likely fail at runtime or produce incorrect results, making the evaluator unable to properly verify the merge requirement
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Replace merge detection logic with: is_merged = any(str(merged_range) == f'{merge_start}:{merge_end}' for merged_range in ws.merged_cells.ranges)
This correctly checks if the specific range 'A1:D1' exists in the merged cell ranges
Alternatively, use: from openpyxl.utils import range_boundaries and check if the merge range matches the expected boundaries
